schema.title: CreateCredentialsRequest
schema.description: The fields of the new credentials.

UserName.description:
The login name. Defaults to the generated `Id`.

A name already in use returns `422`. A reserved name, such as `admin`, `root` or `support`,
returns `400`. Check a name first if it matters to you.

Alias.description: A label shown in the dashboard. Defaults to the login name.

Permission.description: What the credentials can do with files under their home and chroot directories. Defaults to `none`, which can connect but sees nothing. Ignored when you send `HomeDirectoryDetails`.

Password.description:
A password of your choosing. Omit it to have one generated, which is recommended.

It must meet your organization's password policy, which sets its length, the kinds of
characters it needs and whether it may appear in a known data breach. The default policy
requires at least 30 characters, including a number and a lowercase letter, not found in a
breach. The maximum is 64 characters. A password that fails returns `400`.

HomeDirectory.description: Where the credentials land after connecting. Defaults to `/home/{UserName}`. Must start with a slash, not end with one, and not contain a variable such as `${...}`.

ChrootDirectory.description: The highest directory the credentials can reach. Defaults to `/`. Set it to the home directory to confine the credentials to it.

HomeDirectoryDetails.description:
Virtual folders to use instead of a home directory, up to 50. Each maps a path the credentials see to a location in your storage, with its own permission.

A very long `Target` can return `400`. If the folders together are too many or too deep for
SFTP and FTPS, the credentials are still created but can sign in only to the web portal, as
`SupportedProtocols` shows.

items.title: VirtualFolder
items.description: One virtual folder: a path the credentials see, mapped to a location in your storage, with its own permission.

Entry.description: The path the credentials see, such as `/inbound`. Must start with a slash and not end with one. If the root `/` is an entry, it must be the only one. Entries can't share a path, contain one another, or contain a variable such as `${...}`.

Target.description: The location in your storage, as a path from the root of your bucket. Must start with a slash and not end with one. Two entries can show the same location only with the same permission.

Type.description: Whether the entry is a folder or a single file. Defaults to `DIRECTORY`. A `FILE` entry can't be the root `/`.

Permission.description: What the credentials can do inside this entry, with the same levels as `Permission` on the credentials. `none` keeps the entry listed but denies everything in it.

Email.description: Where web portal invitations and password resets are sent. Omit it for credentials used only by a machine. The address starts unverified.

State.description: Set to `inactive` to create the credentials disabled. Any other value creates them `active`.

ExpiresAt.description:
When access stops, in **Unix epoch seconds**. Must be after the end of today and at most a year away. Omit it for credentials that don't expire.

When the time passes, the credentials become `inactive` and `ExpiresAt` returns to `null`.

typical.summary: Named credentials for a specific system
